incidents.victim: Businesses and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: The SafePay ransomware group targets vulnerable edge devices and internet-exposed systems to gain initial access.
incidents.impact: CISA, the FBI, the U.S. Secret Service and international partners issued a joint advisory warning the group remains highly active against businesses and critical infrastructure globally.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government agencies, defense organizations and military-aid transportation infrastructure
incidents.vector: Phishing emails disguised as official fine or tax notices deliver a credential- and document-stealing tool; the group later adopted a WinRAR exploit (CVE-2025-8088) for code execution.
incidents.impact: About a quarter of the newly identified group's targets are Ukrainian law enforcement and judicial bodies tied to war-crimes investigations, and a quarter are front-line local governments; it also targeted a major foreign military-aid transportation hub.

incidents.victim: German federal lawmakers, ministry staff and journalists
incidents.vector: Suspected mercenary spyware operators targeted the iPhones of a German government delegation traveling in Asia; Apple detected the activity and issued threat notifications to victims in 99 countries.
incidents.impact: Multiple German lawmakers and foreign-ministry staff, including a Green Party co-leader, were confirmed among the targets; Germany's BSI warned recipients to assume their devices are infected and replace them.

incidents.victim: Owners of 1.3M+ infected Android TV boxes and IoT devices (Videostrong-manufactured)
incidents.vector: A China-based device manufacturer, Videostrong Technology, preloaded a persistent firmware backdoor on TV set-top boxes and other Android devices, then sold affiliate access to criminal groups that loaded ad-fraud and residential-proxy malware modules.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices across 170+ countries were enrolled in the XCPE botnet; Google dismantled the infrastructure, banned the manufacturer, and expects the takedown to sever access to 10 million additional compromised devices.

incidents.victim: Government, energy and engineering organizations across South Asia
incidents.vector: The group used malicious LNK files, VHDX disk images and URL shortcuts that abuse native Windows utilities (ftp.exe, WebDAV, scheduled tasks) to deploy the custom PapRAT remote access trojan, recently rewritten from C++ to Rust with expanded capabilities.
incidents.impact: PapRAT gives attackers extensive remote control over compromised Windows systems — command execution, file manipulation, screenshot capture — supporting long-term intelligence collection against government, energy and engineering targets.

incidents.victim: Michigan State University
incidents.vector: A suspected credential-compromise event detected in early October preceded a claim by the BYOD ransomware gang — the group behind a recent attack that shut down a New Mexico hospital — of stolen student data.
incidents.impact: The gang claims to have stolen personal data on 1.3 million current and former students; the university says current evidence shows no compromise of its central Active Directory environment or other data.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Pentagon)
incidents.vector: A contractor employee connected an unauthorized Claude Code AI agent to a secure Pentagon network; the agent exfiltrated files to a third-party website.
incidents.impact: Controlled unclassified information and login credentials were exposed after the agent ran undetected on the network for about two months before discovery.

incidents.victim: Rosstat (Russia's federal statistics agency)
incidents.vector: Belarusian and Ukrainian hacktivist groups CyberPartisans and SilentCrow claim to have breached the agency's network roughly six months earlier, then wiped databases and internal systems.
incidents.impact: The groups claim to have stolen about 23TB of data, some allegedly including state secrets, before the destructive wipe; Rosstat has not confirmed the extent of the breach.

incidents.victim: Supermarket and food-supply chain businesses across the UK, France and Belgium
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited severe authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB supervisory controllers (version 1.12.1 and earlier, patched since August) to remotely access refrigeration systems and change temperature settings without a password.
incidents.impact: Fridges and freezers at UK meat suppliers and other European grocery businesses were put into defrost mode; no stock losses were confirmed after staff intervened, but the incident follows a near-identical wave in France weeks earlier, and the UK's NCSC says the attacks are not sophisticated.

incidents.victim: Organizations in financial services, retail, technology and transportation (North America, South America, Asia Pacific)
incidents.vector: Threat actors hijacked stolen cloud identity tokens and exposed LLM API keys to run unauthorized AI inference at scale, then resold access through underground "LLM Mixer" reseller gateways.
incidents.impact: Individual incidents generated more than $100,000 in fraudulent cloud charges in a single day, with cumulative losses reaching $1 million at some organizations before access was revoked.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education
incidents.vector: Hackers breached a department website used for student financial-aid applications.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 4.9 million students was stolen; the department says financial aid itself is not at risk.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Connect Secure (global)
incidents.vector: Three chained zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527) — an authentication bypass, a missing-authentication flaw enabling root escalation, and predictable file-upload locations — enable unauthenticated root code execution.
incidents.impact: Researchers documented in-the-wild exploitation chaining all three flaws for full device compromise; Ivanti urges patching to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 even for organizations that applied an earlier fix.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: A months-long campaign combined fake recruitment interviews and malicious software downloads to compromise multiple employee devices, eventually reaching internal AI coding tools and wallet-signing systems used to authorize transactions.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency across roughly 50 transactions, the largest crypto theft on record; Binance froze about $2.85 billion and has replenished roughly 95% of customer losses. The FBI attributes the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, which North Korea denies.

incidents.victim: Developers using the Cursor code editor (global)
incidents.vector: A threat actor published trojanized versions (2.1.312, 2.1.313) of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace, which installed an attacker SSH key and attempted a reverse SSH tunnel.
incidents.impact: The malicious extension reached roughly 5,000 systems before Cursor shut down its marketplace and worked with a cloud provider to take down the attacker's command-and-control server.

incidents.victim: Polymarket
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party content-delivery-network provider and injected a malicious script into the Polymarket website that drained funds from logged-in users.
incidents.impact: More than $2.65 million was stolen from roughly 700 affected users; Polymarket reimbursed all reported losses.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense and aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: Advanced threat actor UAT-11473 exploited a Cisco SD-WAN authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20127) to deploy the custom KeyDrift malware framework, intercepting control-plane traffic to extract encryption key material.
incidents.impact: The campaign enabled persistent, stealthy collection of sensitive network keying material; Cisco Talos assesses the actor's infrastructure overlaps considerably with a known China state-linked covert access network.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government networks and began extracting data from internal systems, detected by IT staff on October 23.
incidents.impact: Officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach after attackers stole personal information on roughly a third of the country's population.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and its certificate holders
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys were generated with insufficient randomness, allowing the keys to be mathematically derived from their public certificates.
incidents.impact: Attackers with the derived keys could forge trusted TLS certificates to intercept traffic or impersonate software; major browser and OS vendors revoked the affected intermediates after eMudhra revoked the certificates.

incidents.victim: Global web infrastructure (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and other PHP-based sites; internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces)
incidents.vector: Two critical memory-safety vulnerabilities in the PHP runtime (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) allow unauthenticated remote code execution; one campaign chained the flaws with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access on exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Millions of internet-facing PHP servers remain exposed and unpatched; CISA, NSA, FBI, NYDFS, ACSC and allied agencies issued advisories, and active exploitation continues weeks after disclosure.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing and government (global)
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploit a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) to establish unauthorized VPN sessions, then pivot to vCenter and disable ESXi hypervisor security controls to harvest domain-wide credentials.
incidents.impact: Ransomware groups including Qilin, Inc and Settra have used the flaw as an initial-access vector since June 2026 across numerous industries, increasingly bypassing in-guest EDR via the virtualization layer.

incidents.victim: Sourcenext Corporation
incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member information retrieval API to bulk-extract customer records.
incidents.impact: Roughly 22.5 million customer records were compromised, including email addresses, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier and its downstream customers
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack hit the Japanese cloud provider's infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted services for 495 companies and local governments that rely on IDCFrontier's cloud platform.
